body:
Could this perhaps be a security issue? The different implementation between signing and verification means that a signed valid URL can be extended with empty query parameters and still be valid. For instance, both URLs below are treated as valid:

https://app.test/signed?a=b&c=d&signature=4064c3c575b1215a1e1272d82cb76ec9d99fa944c2f0902b8456ce97df863882

https://app.test/signed?a=b&c=d&signature=4064c3c575b1215a1e1272d82cb76ec9d99fa944c2f0902b8456ce97df863882&some&more&params



I think the problem (if it is a problem and not by design) is related to the fact that `http_build_query` ignores `null` values.

I don't feel confident enough to make a PR, but here's a POC for an alternative implementation that passes all existing tests, including new ones to test for empty parameters as well as the possible security issue of being able to append additional key-only parameters.

https://github.com/Krisell/framework/pull/1/files
We're a bit confused here. Is the issue now that the url is not validated (as @jelib3an indicates) or that it is validated (as @Krisell indicates)?

To be more specific, a url of `https://app.test/2?order=asc&reverse` would be treated as

`https://app.test/2?order=asc&reverse` by the signer
`https://app.test/2?order=asc` by the validator

Resulting in different signatures.

The fact that the validator ignores part of the data also means that any valid signature url `https://SignedURL` is still valid when used as `https://SignedURL&some&additional&parameters&which&depending&on&the&implementation&could&have&effect`

@Krisell Thanks for investigating! Nice find too on the secondary issue. Your patch works for `?param` but not for the empty string case `?param=`. Not sure if that's a case we want to support but it will require modifying code within `signedRoute()` as well... Regardless, your patch is already an improvement. 

Also, just taking a step back and thinking about this issue as a whole, is this something that should be addressed by Symfony instead?
Signed URLs is not a Symfony feature.
If someone wants to PR a change in behavior for the empty parameter thing feel free.

> Signed URLs is not a Symfony feature.

Sorry, I meant whether Symfony should make the differentiation within `$request->query()` since at the moment both "value-less" and empty string values come back as null.

@jelib3an Perhaps we can work out a solution together, feel free to contact me on my email (which you can see on my profile page) or the Laravel Discord.

I agree that it might be problematic that missing and empty values are indistinguishable in the request data, but we might be able to work around that by inspecting the raw URI?
